page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is built on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 48 MB of Level 3 cache along with instruction set support for AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions including AES and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmarks demonstrate stable memory throughput, reaching 126.91 GB/sec on large-block uncached sequential reads and 58.65 GB/sec on writes. Local storage is not bundled, meaning all persistent data relies on remote network block storage. Networking capability is backed by a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating sustained data transfer volumes across internal cloud infrastructure.

Benchmark evaluations place general computing throughput within standard expectations for its hardware generation, scoring 34961.9 on PassMark CPU, 1502.0 on Geekbench single-core, and 12846.0 on Geekbench multi-core. In application-specific testing, the instance achieved 24585.0 in Clang compilation and handled 28.45 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference showed distinct competence, delivering 266.46 tokens per second during text generation on small 135M parameter language models.

Given the balanced allocation of raw compute and moderate memory without attached local NVMe disks, ecs.c7.8xlarge offers solid cost efficiency for CPU-bound pipelines that do not require high per-core RAM density. Optimal production workloads include multi-threaded software build pipelines, batch data processing, web serving clusters, Redis caching nodes, and quantized CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 64.0 GB of system memory, it maintains a strict 1:2 core-to-memory profile. The platform lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, while providing 16 Gbps of baseline networking capacity. Compute benchmarks show solid mid-range performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 34961.9 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 12846.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 126.91 GB/sec on large-block reads, and Redis SET throughput clocks at 28.45 million operations per second. Supported by AVX-512 VNNI vector extensions, it performs strongly in small-model text generation inference. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation, batch transformations, caching layers, and high-concurrency web application serving.
